extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and activists seeking to petition the Pulitzer Board to revoke Walter Duranty’s Pulitzer Prize (advocates, journalists, scholars, and concerned citizens)
extracted.subtask_description: A campaign-style how-to/missional page arguing for revocation of Walter Duranty’s 1932 Pulitzer Prize by documenting false reporting, mobilizing public engagement (petitions/letters), and presenting supporting evidence and precedent for rescission. It guides advocacy actions and states the standards Duranty failed to meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Pulitzer Prize standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pulitzer Prize is a distinguished and highly coveted award given to deserving journalists who stake their reputation on the truth. Duranty 'did not live up to any standards of the award.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the reporting meets the Prize’s implied standards of truthful, rigorous journalism; use the Prize’s mission as the baseline when arguing for revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / Accuracy of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Duranty 'spread false news worldwide' and there is 'over 20 years of evidence of falsifications of truth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document specific factual falsifications and demonstrate how Duranty’s reports were false; compile evidence (e.g., 'Duranty Smoking Gun', related documentation) showing inaccurate or fabricated reporting as the basis for challenging the Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoddy journalism / lack of journalistic integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission statement cites 'shoddy journalism' as a reason the Prize should be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show patterns of poor reporting practice (lack of verification, reliance on unreliable sources, ignoring available evidence) and contrast Duranty’s methods with accepted journalistic standards to establish unfitness for the Prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of an oppressive regime / propagandistic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Duranty 'promoted the legitimacy of the Soviet Union' rather than exercising independent journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that reporting that functions as propaganda — i.e., promoting a regime’s legitimacy or failing to challenge atrocities — violates the ethical expectations for Pulitzer-winning journalism; provide examples where Duranty’s reporting served Soviet interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of evidentiary documentation and historical record
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists 'Related Documentation' (letters, fact sheets, 'smoking gun' pieces, sample op-eds) as the basis for the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather, cite, and present documentary evidence (archival material, contemporaneous reports, scholarly work like The Holodomor Reader) to substantiate claims of falsification and misconduct when petitioning the Pulitzer Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent for revocation / institutional responsibility to act
rubrics_metrics.description: The page questions why the Pulitzer Committee, 'after over 20 years of evidence of falsifications of truth, shoddy journalism and precedence of revocation, still does not want to do the right thing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making a case for revocation, point to prior instances where awards have been rescinded (precedent) and argue the Board’s duty to apply consistent standards; use precedent to strengthen the moral and procedural case for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and organized advocacy (petitions, letters, media outreach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The campaign urges readers to 'SIGN THE PETITION', offers 'Sample Pulitzer Letter 1/2' and 'Sample Op-Ed Duranty Revocation', and provides media contacts for inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobilize public support through petitions, coordinated letter-writing to the Pulitzer Board and editors, and media outreach using provided sample texts; treat public pressure and informed outreach as tactical criteria for influencing the Board.
